findings.F1: The tested measure is zero, not merely short of the bar. The mean 18-bar unusual move of the 4537 long cases is +0.0003 % with t 0.002. At 6 bars it is +0.066 % (t 0.98) and at 12 bars +0.013 % (t 0.13), so no horizon from one to three days shows the pooled effect.
findings.F2: The rebound appears only in the largest losses relative to the usual move. The top decile of the streak's loss in usual moves (mean 5.9 usual moves, 422 cases) has a mean 18-bar unusual move of +2.03 % (t 4.18), and the ninth decile (3.3 usual moves) has +0.75 % (t 1.95). Deciles 0 to 6 (0.4 to 2.0 usual moves) are all at or below zero, between −0.32 % and −0.93 %, with the second decile at t −2.80. Over the whole set, the forecast's above-median minus below-median difference is +1.07 %.
findings.F3: The top quintile of relative loss (at least 2.8 usual moves, 843 cases) gives a clear and stable result. Its mean 18-bar unusual move is +1.39 % (t 4.48), a strength of 0.165. It is also positive at 6 bars (+0.71 %, t 3.93) and at 12 bars (+0.97 %, t 3.61). It is positive in all six coins, from LTC's +0.32 % (t 0.53) to ZEC's +2.37 % (t 2.31). It is positive in 6 of 8 years; the exceptions are 2018 (−0.34 %) and 2022 (−1.06 %).
findings.F4: In the pooled cases, the market's own moves drown the effect. The cases' 18-bar unusual move swings by year, from −1.46 % (t −3.47) in 2018 and −1.25 % (t −3.95) in 2022 to +1.40 % (t 3.25) in 2021. The top quintile, by contrast, holds in both 30-day trends: +1.49 % (t 3.51, 500 cases) after a falling month and +1.25 % (t 2.79, 343 cases) after a rising one.
findings.F5: The fading volume the idea requires adds little to the large-loss rebound. Among all down-streaks recomputed from prices, the top relative-loss quintile gives +1.41 % over 18 bars with fading volume (t 2.88, 423 cases) and +1.02 % with rising volume (t 2.91, 634 cases). Over 6 bars the order reverses: +0.27 % (t 1.04) with fading volume against +0.63 % (t 2.70) with rising volume.
findings.F6: Most cases are small streaks that carry nothing. 3747 of the 4537 cases are two-bar streaks, with a mean of −0.04 % (t −0.29). The forecast ranks the outcome no better than the raw loss does (Spearman correlation with the 18-bar move 0.076 against 0.083 for the raw loss in usual moves), because it standardises against its own recent values.
findings.F7: In its large-loss part, the idea's move covers the cost of a trade many times over. The top quintile's total 18-bar move per case is +1.80 %, about 9 times the 0.19 % a trade cost, against 0.41 % (2.1 times) for all cases.

ideas.idea: When a coin has just fallen in an unbroken streak of four-hour periods, and the volume across the streak has been declining, it rises over the next three days, only when the streak's loss is several times the coin's typical four-hour move over the past 30 days. Beyond that, the larger the loss relative to that typical move, the larger the rise.
ideas.consequence: A trader buys only the down-streaks that are extreme against the coin's usual four-hour move, and refuses the common short ones, which give nothing back.
ideas.name: extreme down-streak rebound only

ideas.idea: When a coin has just fallen in an unbroken streak of four-hour periods whose loss is several times its typical four-hour move over the past 30 days, it rises over the next one to three days, whatever the volume did during the streak. The larger the loss relative to that typical move, the larger the rise.
ideas.consequence: A trader can buy into an extreme down-streak's rebound without waiting for volume to fade, which roughly doubles the number of opportunities.
ideas.name: extreme down-streak rebound, any volume
